narration.full_text: Namaste students! It's time to test your understanding of Control and Coordination with a quick quiz. Let's see how well you've grasped the concepts we've discussed. Get ready to answer some thought-provoking questions! First question: Write three main functions of the nervous system. What are the key roles it plays in our body? Think about how it helps us interact with our environment. Next up, we have a question about the neuron. (a) Draw the structure of a neuron and label the cell body and axon. (b) Name the part of the neuron: (i) Where the information is acquired. (ii) Through which information travels as an electrical impulse. Now, let's consider the protection of our vital organs. 'Brain and Spinal cord are two vital organs of our body'. How is our body designed to protect them? Think about the structures that safeguard these crucial parts of our central nervous system. Finally, let's define some important terms. (i) Define receptor and state their location in our body. Mention any two receptors present in our forebrain and their functions. (ii) How do nerve impulses travel in our body? This question covers both definition and process. Take your time to recall the details.

visual_beats.description: Title: Test Your Knowledge! Control and Coordination

Question: 17. Write three main functions of the nervous system. Answer: (i) Collects information from the surroundings. (ii) Controls and co-ordinates the movement of muscles. (iii) Helps to recognise smell, taste, vision, hearing etc. with the help of sense organs.

Question: 18. (a) Draw the structure of neuron and label cell body and axon. (b) Name the part of neuron: (i) Where the information is acquired. (ii) Through which information travels as an electrical impulse. Answer: (a) [Diagram of a neuron] (b) (i) The information is acquired at the end of the dendrite tip of a nerve cell (ii) The information travels as an electrical impulse from the dendrite to the cell body and then along the axon to its end.

Question: 19. 'Brain and Spinal cord are two vital organs of our body'. How is our body designed to protect them? Answer: Brain is located inside a bony box, named as cranium and a fluid is present in this balloon, known as cerebrospinal fluid which is a shock absorber. Spinal cord is placed in a vertebral column and back bone protects it.

Question: 20. (i) Define receptor and state their location in our body. Mention any two receptors present in our forebrain and their functions (ii) How do nerve impulses travel in our body? Answer: (i) Specialised tips of some nerve cells which receive information from the surroundings are receptor. Location: Sense organs. Gustatory receptor: Detect taste. Olfactory receptor: Detect smell. (ii) The information acquired at the end of the dendritic tip of a nerve cell, sets off a chemical reaction that creates an electrical impulse, which travels to the cell body, then along the axon to its end, releases some chemicals, across the synapses.
